Change a rule's fields from flags, or the keys a rule file holds

## Usage

```text
chainmail rule edit <id|name> (field flags | -f FILE) [flags]
```

## Examples

```sh
chainmail rule edit receipts --priority 10 --stop
chainmail rule edit inbox-cleanup --at 07:00
# change only the keys the file holds
chainmail rule edit receipts -f receipts.toml
```

## Flags

```text
      --account stringArray     an account the rule covers (repeatable; default: every account)
      --action stringArray      an action, run in the order given (repeatable): label=NAME, unlabel=NAME, copy=FOLDER, move=FOLDER, link_item=ID[,anchor], forward=ADDR[,ADDR...], flag, unflag, read, unread, archive or trash
      --all-accounts            make the rule cover every account
      --at string               run once a day at this time, HH:MM in the [rules] timezone
      --description string      what the rule is for
      --every string            run on a schedule, this long after the last run finished: 15m to 30d, such as 6h or 7d
      --expected-revision int   refuse the change if the rule is no longer at this revision
  -f, --file string             read the rule from this TOML rule file instead of the field flags
      --max-per-run int32       the most messages one run acts on, 1 to 5000 (default 500)
      --name string             the rule's name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit
      --no-schedule             take the rule off its schedule
      --note string             the note the forward action adds above the forwarded message
      --on-new                  run on new mail as the cache takes it
      --priority int32          order among rules, lowest first, -1000000 to 1000000 (default 100)
      --query string            the messages to act on, in the search language
      --stop                    keep later rules off the messages this rule matched
```

## Global flags

```text
      --output string   output format: json or table (default $CHAINMAIL_OUTPUT, then cli.toml, then table on a terminal, json otherwise)
      --socket string   daemon socket (default $CHAINMAIL_SOCKET, then cli.toml, then /run/chainmail/chainmail.sock)
```
